item.title: World reacts to Democrats' midterm elections victory
item.description: From Kyiv to Moscow, and Tehran to Tel Aviv, all eyes were on the Democrats big win on Wednesday, as foreign powers weigh up how a flipped Congress will impact international relations.

item.title: Democrats seize full control of Congress. And, which candidates made history last night
item.description: Democrats have won the House and the Senate, taking full control of Congress for the first time since 2023. And history was made in several states. Here's what happened last night.

item.title: Japan faces diplomatic dilemma amid joint pressure from nuclear neighbors
item.description: As the Ukraine war grinds on, ties between Russia and neighboring Japan are at their worst in decades. Tokyo wants more support from Washington, but some Japanese are concerned they may not get it.

item.title: For Ukraine's Kherson region, a short ceasefire meant a momentary return to normal life
item.description: In Kherson city, usually seething with Russian drones, friends met at cafes, families were out together and shoppers stocked up. "The city seems alive," said one resident, "just like it used to be."

item.description: Russia launched 289 attack drones, 17 ballistic missiles and 59 cruise missiles across nine regions, President Zelenskyy said in an online post that noted the barrage coincided with U.S. elections.

item.title: Haley Stevens backs Mike Rogers. And, Gulf states brace for potential attack on Iran
item.description: Democrats in Michigan are considering their options after Haley Stevens endorsed GOP candidate Mike Rogers for Senate. And the Gulf states are bracing for a possible U.S. attack on Iran after the midterms.

item.title: Hundreds evacuate city during temporary ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine
item.description: The ceasefire in a Russian-occupied Ukrainian city has ended. The ceasefire, which lasted several days, allowed hundreds of residents to evacuate.

item.title: UN's peacekeeping mission in disputed Western Sahara ends after 35 years
item.description: The U.N.'s long-running peacekeeping mission for the disputed Western Sahara ceased operations Sunday after 35 years. Once ruled by Spain, it is claimed by both Morocco and the pro-independence Polisario Front.
